chapter: Union, Emmett Hardy and Rampart Street Parade
title: Emmett Hardy's style, and the Bee Palmer vaudeville tour
summary: He describes Emmett Hardy's playing as close to Bix, and mentions the vaudeville tour with Santo and Johnny Frisco.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Emmett Hardy? What kind of style did he have?
Well, he, he had a style more, more like Big Spider-Back.

And, and, and it's kind of hard to, to explain. I mean, I, I don't know notes. You understand? Mm-hmm. I mean, I know how to read drum music, but I don't know notes up and down the scale. I studied out there with Earl Hatchett, trying to, trying to learn how to play vibrapholes and stuff like that. But I, I, I could memorize things better and, and, and play it my own way. Mm-hmm. Faster than I could read it. See, I, I'm, I'm slow at reading anything, besides music, you know. So, uh, Emmett Hardy, he just, had, had a certain way of playing. I mean, it's too bad that, that you didn't get a chance to, to, to talk to, what's the name, before you passed away. Piano player. You told me about, about, uh, Brian Lee? Yeah.

Well, I mean, he, he, he would be able to tell you more about it, see. Or, Bill Eastwood. Yeah, I knew him too. Because they, they lived over there in Al Jays, you know, I mean, uh, Eastwood and, and they played, uh, with, uh, well, he played at the halfway house when I was there, see. But, uh, but Emmett, uh, they went on, uh, on a tour. He, I don't, uh, Johnny Frisco drummed up, let's see if I can remember this guy. Johnny Frisco was on drums, Santo, Emmett Hardy, and, uh, I don't know, Harry Shields or Larry Shields or, or, or Branny. There was, you know, they were supposed to be the jazz clowns, like, with, uh, Pete Palmer.
I don't know whether they know about that, ever heard about that.
Yeah, Santo told me about it.
Oh, Santo, yeah. Well, that's it. Well, that, that's, that's a thing.
